items.comparator: No comparator stated; the release says the system screened compounds and identified candidates, but gives no baseline or comparison group.
items.quantitative_outcome: CATL reported: “The system has enabled CATL to screen more than 1,600 compounds and identify seven promising candidate materials in a short time.” It also said the system draws on “600 TB of data and more than one trillion testing data points.”

items.company: Tempus AI / Pathos AI / Bristol Myers Squibb
items.signal: Tempus agreed to provide Pathos with a de-identified longitudinal dataset drawn from hundreds of thousands of people with neurological conditions under a five-year, $55 million data-licensing agreement. BMS is also involved and was reported to receive limited exclusivity through the arrangement. This is a distinctive data-access move, not a measured operating benefit.
items.source: PharmExec, reporting the companies’ collaborations and citing the Pathos AI announcement

items.signal: BMS agreed to license Tempus multimodal oncology data through 2031 and gain access to Tempus’ Lens platform. The announcement describes data and platform access for drug discovery and development, but reports no measured outcome.
items.source: Tempus AI press release, as reproduced by BioSpace

items.signal: The companies announced a non-binding collaboration to explore use of AI and real-world data for clinical-trial matching and related care workflows, with an initial hypertension program in Abu Dhabi involving M42. No measured operating benefit was reported; this is an early-stage data/workflow collaboration rather than demonstrated advantage.

A multi-year collaboration will connect PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing with Verily’s clinical data platform to create clinico-genomic datasets for biomedical research and AI model training. No measured outcome or comparison was stated; the potential signal is access to combined genomic and clinical data.

items.quantitative_outcome: AI-enabled workflows reduced trade-document processing turnaround times by over 70%.
items.signal: Trade-document processing turnaround time reportedly fell by over 70% with AI-enabled workflows. The cited report does not state the comparison period or baseline.

items.quantitative_outcome: The bank reports about 30 minutes saved per Copilot user per day; transfers of calls between staff in its contact centre fell by more than 40%.
items.signal: Bank of Ireland reported average daily time saved among Copilot users and a reduction in contact-centre call transfers. The cited brief gives no baseline, measurement method, or quality measure.

items.quantitative_outcome: none stated. The company says Veeam events will be analyzed alongside “more than 10 trillion security events processed each week across customer environments”; this describes the platform’s event volume, not a measured improvement from the integration.
items.signal: Partnership integrates Veeam backup and recovery events—including malware detections, suspicious user behavior, unauthorized restore attempts, failed backups, and administrative changes—with Arctic Wolf’s security operations platform. This is a distinctive data-access move that may broaden its threat context; no outcome from the integration is yet quantified.
items.source: Arctic Wolf and Veeam press release, issued by Arctic Wolf

items.signal: Orange Cyberdefense describes a proprietary, autonomous threat knowledge base and an agent-based layer in its operational model, with Qevlar AI integrated into SOCs in France and internationally. Potentially differentiated data and operating capability, but the article gives no measured benefit or comparison.
